capabilities.name: Code Review
capabilities.description: Peer review of Source Code changes before merge.

items.statement: Use .editorconfig to setup your editor
Use 2 spaces for indenting your code
Clean up any trailing whitespace in your JS files before committing.
Use semicolons; linebreaks don't terminate statements in javascript
Use single quotes, unless you are writing JSON.
Opening braces go on the same line as the statement.
Use lowerCamelCase for variables, properties and function names.
Use UpperCamelCase for class names.
Use UPPERCASE for Constants.
Use the === operator for conditionals.
The ternary operator should not be used on a single line. Split it up into multiple lines instead.
Any non-trivial conditions should be assigned to a descriptively named variable or function.
To avoid deep nesting of if-statements, always return a function's value as early as possible.
Name your closures. Use closures, but don't nest them.
One method per line should be used if you want to chain methods. You should also indent these methods so it's easier to tell they are part of the same chain.

Use slashes for both single line and multi line comments. Try to write comments that explain higher level mechanisms or clarify difficult segments of your code. Don't use comments to restate trivial things.
Always put requires at top of file to clearly illustrate a file's dependencies.
Do not extend built-in prototypes.
sync and npm-check to automate the task of identifying insecure and outdated components.
Using Async-Await or promises for async error handling
Is there a separation between operational vs programmer errors
Are errors handled centrally? Instead of middlewares
Removing unwanted dependencies which are not being used in the project.
All the commonly used functions should be in utils file of helper folder.
Avoid using var, and promote use of let and const.
Make sure that sensitive data are saved on .env files and are used from that on projects.
Input validation
Use of HELMET package middleware to avoid common security issues in the app
Error messages should be generic.
Using bcrpyt module for storing passwords securely
Using and configuring PM2 so that if any failure occur it get restarted automatically
Always enable monitoring and logging for the node app in case where we want to debug the application on failure
Rate limiting the end points.
Try to make the code more functional. (Use of modular styling of code)
DB connections & file operation like streaming should be properly closed.
If using multiple DB queries/calls within a block of code which are independent of each other then they can be wrapped in Promise.all
Proper commenting should be followed for each and every API
Make sure DB queries uses indexes for maximize performance.
Before using any third party packages make sure it is frequently updated and developer support is also there.
Code indentation by using Prettier or Beautify.
Schedule a good backup strategy for your production DB in any chance of failure
While using $unwind stage make sure to enable option preserveNullAndEmptyArrays so that any document with empty array doesn’t get skip.
Use explain stage while writing big queries to see how well the query is performing
Use of $match, $limit & $skip can filter out most of the documents if used on a early pipeline stage.
